services.note: Software, IT services, cloud and data. India holds about 8% of the EU's imports from outside the EU.

services.note: India's sales grew 17% a year, about three times the market.

rules.title: Carbon border tax (CBAM) on iron and steel
rules.text: Iron and steel (HS 72 and many HS 73 lines, including fasteners) and aluminium are in scope. The definitive regime has applied since 1 January 2026. Certificates go on sale on 1 February 2027, and the first annual declaration (for 2026 imports) is due on 30 September 2027. The EU importer needs verified emissions data from the Indian producer.

rules.title: CE marking for machinery
rules.text: Machinery sold in the EU needs CE marking under the Machinery Directive 2006/42/EC, replaced by the Machinery Regulation (EU) 2023/1230, which applies from 20 January 2027.

rules.title: Pressure equipment (valves, fittings, vessels)
rules.text: Pressure Equipment Directive 2014/68/EU: conformity assessment, with a notified body for the higher-risk categories, and CE marking.

rules.title: Automotive parts: buyer and type-approval requirements
rules.text: European carmakers and tier-1 suppliers expect IATF 16949 certification. Regulated parts (lighting, brakes, glazing and others) need UNECE type approval.

rules.title: Steel import quotas
rules.text: The steel safeguard ended on 30 June 2026. Since 1 July 2026, Regulation (EU) 2026/1384 sets tariff-free quotas about 47% below 2024 levels and a 50% duty on imports above the quota, on top of normal duties.

rules.title: REACH registration and CLP labelling
rules.text: Every substance placed on the EU market at 1 tonne a year or more must be registered under REACH, which a non-EU maker does through an EU-based Only Representative. Classification and labelling follow CLP.

rules.title: Active pharmaceutical ingredients
rules.text: APIs need EU GMP and, for each shipment's source site, a written confirmation from the exporting country's regulator (India: CDSCO), under the Falsified Medicines Directive 2011/62/EU.

rules.title: Finished medicines
rules.text: A marketing authorisation (EU-wide or national), EU GMP inspection of the plant, and serialisation under the falsified-medicines rules.

rules.title: Agrochemicals
rules.text: Active substances must be approved under Regulation (EC) 1107/2009, and treated produce must meet EU maximum residue levels.

rules.title: Carbon border tax (CBAM) on fertilisers, ammonia and hydrogen
rules.text: Fertilisers, ammonia and hydrogen are also in CBAM scope; other chemicals, APIs and medicines are not.

rules.title: Tariffs on Indian textiles and apparel
rules.text: Indian apparel pays about 9 to 12% in the EU, while Bangladesh pays zero (its preference continues to 2029 after it leaves least-developed status in November 2026). The EU–India agreement is expected to remove these tariffs once in force. In the UK, the UK–India agreement has applied since 15 July 2026. Exact rates per product come from Access2Markets in the build.

rules.title: Chemical restrictions in textiles and leather
rules.text: REACH Annex XVII restricts azo dyes, chromium VI in leather and other substances. A broad restriction on PFAS chemicals has been proposed and is under evaluation by the European Chemicals Agency.

rules.title: Textile labelling
rules.text: Fibre-composition labels under the Textile Labelling Regulation (EU) 1007/2011.

rules.title: Ecodesign and unsold-goods rules
rules.text: The Ecodesign for Sustainable Products Regulation (EU) 2024/1781 names textiles among the first product groups. Since 19 July 2026 large companies may not destroy unsold apparel, clothing accessories or footwear; medium-sized companies follow in 2030.

rules.title: Deforestation rules for cattle leather
rules.text: The EU Deforestation Regulation (EU) 2023/1115 covers cattle leather and requires due diligence on origin. After two postponements it applies from 30 December 2026 for large operators and 30 June 2027 for micro and small ones.

rules.title: Forced labour ban
rules.text: Products made with forced labour are banned from the EU market under Regulation (EU) 2024/3015, which applies from 14 December 2027.

rules.title: Personal data transfers (GDPR)
rules.text: There is no EU adequacy decision for India, so personal data sent to India needs standard contractual clauses and a transfer impact assessment.

rules.title: AI Act
rules.text: The AI Act (EU) 2024/1689 bans some practices, and its general-purpose AI duties are already in force. Under the Digital Omnibus agreed in May 2026, high-risk duties move to 2 December 2027 (standalone systems) and 2 August 2028 (systems in products). The page mentions the delay only once it is published in the Official Journal.

rules.title: Security duties passed to IT suppliers (NIS2, DORA)
rules.text: NIS2 (Directive (EU) 2022/2555) and, for financial clients, DORA (Regulation (EU) 2022/2554, applying since 17 January 2025) push security, audit and contract requirements onto ICT suppliers.

rules.title: Onsite staff in Europe
rules.text: Staff working at client sites need intra-corporate transfer permits (Directive 2014/66/EU) or an EU Blue Card. India has social security agreements with 12 EU countries (Austria, Belgium, Czechia, Denmark, Finland, France, Germany, Hungary, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Portugal, Sweden), so posted staff avoid double contributions there; Italy, Spain, Poland and Ireland are not covered. The UK's agreement applies since 15 July 2026.

src.label: Lok Sabha answer, India's social security agreements

rules.title: UK–India trade agreement
rules.text: The UK–India Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement entered into force on 15 July 2026, together with a convention that spares posted workers double social-security contributions for up to five years.

rules.title: EU–India trade agreement
rules.text: Negotiations concluded in January 2026 and the Commission sent the signature proposal to the Council in September 2026. Signing is reported for around December 2026; until it enters into force the EU's standard tariffs apply. The page states the expected timing only as reported, never as fact.
